title: Chess, But My Knights Are Trojan Horses...
summary: Chess vs (Fairy-)Stockfish where White's two knights are Trojan Horses: as a move, a Trojan knight can disperse into up to nine white pawns filling the 3x3 block centred on its square (only vacant squares get pawns; the knight itself becomes the centre pawn). Narrator rushes a knight to c6 early, disperses a wall of pawns into Black's camp (net +6 points per knight), forks with b7, and eventually wins with a ladder mate.
rules: Standard chess start; player White vs Stockfish (3600). Only White's two knights are Trojan Horses.

A Trojan knight moves as a knight, or (as the player's move) disperses: it is replaced by white pawns on every vacant square of the 3x3 block centred on it, including its own square; occupied squares are skipped.
Dispersing removes the knight; it is a one-time action per knight.
Pawns created behave as normal white pawns (move toward rank 8, promote); pawns created on rank 8 presumably promote/are invalid [not stated].
Avoid knight trades: a captured Trojan can't disperse.
